title: A Asset for the Ghost
premise: Cyrus Brightwater, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office—an embassy that exists on no map—takes a routine job scrubbing a passenger manifest and watches the entire flight record evaporate mid-air, along with everyone aboard. The vanished plane carried a courier holding 'the Ledger,' a memory archive that can prove which governments manufactured the crisis, and Cyrus's own erased past is buried inside it. Hunted by their own office, a rival syndicate, and the flight's sole survivor—a child who remembers everything—Cyrus must decide whether to trade the Ledger for their safety or expose it and burn every ghost including themselves. In the end Cyrus trades the secret worth killing for: their own identity, surrendered to save the survivor, walking away nameless but finally unowned.
about_author: R. M. Eastwick is the pen name of a former intelligence-adjacent analyst who spent a decade writing briefings no one was meant to read. They now write thrillers about the people history is written around.

chapters.title: The Unlisted Door
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus Brightwater. A quiet Tuesday in Vienna: Cyrus erases a diplomat's indiscretion from three databases before lunch, establishing their craft, their handler Voss, and the Meridian Office's gray existence. Emotional beat: competent loneliness—the ease of deleting lives while having none of their own.

chapters.title: Manifest of No One
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Handed a routine job: sanitize the manifest of Flight 447-Carpathian before landing. Mid-task, the flight record vanishes globally—radar, bookings, even the airline's memory of it. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into dread as Cyrus realizes they were the last hand touching it.

chapters.title: What the Tower Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus visits the control tower; controllers genuinely don't remember the flight, though one keeps humming a song from its in-flight playlist without knowing why. First hint the disappearance is memory-based, not digital. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past itself has been edited.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Boarded
chapters.summary: POV alternating to Ilse, an eleven-year-old stowaway found hiding in a freight depot, clutching a cold case marked with the Meridian seal. She remembers the flight perfectly. Emotional beat: wary tenderness as Cyrus recognizes a fellow person the system tried to erase.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Inside the case: the Ledger, an encrypted neural archive containing verifiable memories—including fragments of Cyrus's own redacted childhood. Voss orders it returned unread. Emotional beat: hunger and fear; the first crack in Cyrus's loyalty.

chapters.title: Orders From Nowhere
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Handler chapters reveal the Office's internal panic: someone above Voss wants the Ledger destroyed and Cyrus retired. Voss hesitates, torn between duty and protectiveness. Emotional beat: institutional corruption shown from inside the machine.

chapters.title: Retirement Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. An assassination attempt disguised as a safehouse transfer; Cyrus survives on instinct and Ilse's warning. They go dark together. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallized—the family that never existed disowns them.

chapters.title: Found Family, Forged Papers
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. On the run through Budapest, Ilse and Cyrus build a fragile domesticity in safehouses—schoolwork at kitchen tables, cover stories like bedtime tales. Emotional beat: warmth blooming in hostile territory; the theme of found family made literal.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Rival broker Sable Antov offers protection and a fortune for the Ledger, revealing a buyer: a coalition of states implicated in the flight's erasure. Emotional beat: temptation framed as rescue—power offering to corrupt gently.

chapters.title: Memory Market
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. In an underground archive bazaar where memories are bought and sold, Ilse glimpses her mother's recorded voice for sale. She steals it rather than buy it back. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve; what memory means when it's property.

chapters.title: Voss Defects
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Ordered to certify Cyrus's termination, Voss instead burns their own file and goes rogue, bringing one asset: proof the Office manufactured the flight's disappearance to bury the Ledger's contents. Emotional beat: redemption sought too late to be clean.

chapters.title: Three Ghosts at a Table
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The trio compares fragments; the Ledger's cipher key is split—half in Cyrus's forgotten childhood, half in Ilse's remembered flight. Trust becomes tactical necessity. Emotional beat: reluctant interdependence hardening into real loyalty.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Gala
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Infiltrating a Zurich charity gala where the buyers convene, Cyrus faces Sable publicly and learns the endgame: not selling the Ledger but detonating it—releasing every archived memory, drowning the guilty and innocent alike. Emotional beat: horror at power's indifference to collateral.

chapters.title: Ilse Taken
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Captured by Sable's crew as leverage, Ilse resists interrogation using the very memories they want—feeding them false ones she authored herself. Emotional beat: agency seized; the child outmaneuvers adults with the truth's shape.

chapters.title: Price of a Name
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Sable's counteroffer: Ilse's life for the Ledger. Cyrus prepares to trade, discovering the final key requires surrendering their own archived self—their identity literally uploaded and erased. Emotional beat: the secret worth killing for turns out to be Cyrus.

chapters.title: Voss's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Cornered by Office retrieval teams, Voss broadcasts the Office's crimes wide enough that suppression would confirm them, buying Cyrus hours at the cost of capture. Emotional beat: sacrifice as apology; a parent-figure's final act.

chapters.title: Exchange at the Terminus
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Midnight rail terminus: the swap. Cyrus hands over the Ledger casing—but Ilse's false-memory gambit means Sable receives a poisoned archive that will unravel the buyers' network from within. Emotional beat: controlled fury; the con within the concession.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Upward
chapters.summary: POV multiple, braided. The poisoned Ledger detonates across the buyers' systems; the Office fractures; Sable realizes the trap as the gala's powerful begin devouring each other. Emotional beat: cathartic chaos—corruption consuming itself.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. To complete the cipher and free Ilse's true memories, Cyrus uploads their own archived past and lets it be wiped—losing their name, history, and the last proof of who they were. Emotional beat: grief and liberation entwined; identity traded for love.

chapters.title: A Person Without Records
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse recovers her full memory—and chooses to keep Cyrus anyway, telling them stories of who they were until new ones take root. Emotional beat: found family completed; memory rebuilt by witness rather than record.

chapters.title: Flight 447-Carpathian
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Weeks later, the world quietly 'remembers' the flight again—rewritten by survivors' testimony seeded by Voss's broadcast. Some passengers are still missing; some answers stay buried. Emotional beat: sober resolution; justice partial, truth negotiated.

chapters.title: The Unlisted Door, Open
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Under a chosen new name, Cyrus opens a small inquiry office that helps the erased reclaim their records. Ilse does homework at the front desk. A knock comes: another ghost needs a fixer. Emotional beat: hopeful ending earned—power renounced, family kept, memory made by choice.
